---
title: "Exploring Old condition data"
cache: TRUE
---

Prior to the WCA project, data was collected WT estate sites, prinicply to inform management decision making at the site or strata scale.

-   Primarily survey data acted as a reference note for individual site managers.

-   The favorability of condition was inferred mainly from the subjective assessment of whether or not management interventions were desirable or practical for each indicators.

-   Notably, the survey employed no structured sampling design, and took a very different approach to the measurement of indicators compared to the WECA plot-based sample approach.

With that in mind - and an appropriately large bowl of salt at hand to mask the overly caveated flavor that must accompany any conclusions, interpretations and comparisons using this data - this document seeks to explore what useful information can be gleaned from this hard-won dataset to assess and report on the historical state of ecological condition on the Woodland Trust Estate.

# Methodological Caveats

## Caveat 1: Measurement of indicators was relatively subjective and assessed at zone level

Using the old method, indicator estimation was primarily at the survey-zone (or "strata") level, rather than within sample plots[^exploring-old-condition-data-1], and that estimation was relatively subjective (as required by a large area covered non-systematically). The Sylva/FC method also typically uses zone-average measurements for many of the indicators.

[^exploring-old-condition-data-1]: Plots were used, but they were optional and not a structured sample or formal estimation process.

## Caveat 2: Plots are not a reliable representation of the zone

The plots (or rather "stops") were not part of a formalised sampling design, but rather intended to act as an optional, informal, and intuition-based aid for estimating indicators at zone level:

-   "*The aim is not to aggregate the information from the plots \[...\] in a strict mathematical way, but to use \[...\] in conjunction with your broader observations from the walk through to make a judgement about these attributes*"
-   *"more for your benefit than as a permanent record"*.
-   "*Some people find these stops more helpful than others: it is not compulsory to use them, and they should not be used as a substitute for observation along the whole length of the walk."*

Plot sizes and locations were not recorded.

## Caveat 3: Varying plot and zone size affect indicator measurements

Plot size was unfixed

-   Guidance suggested *"a rough boundary of, say 10 or 20m"*.

Woodland zone/strata also obviously varied in size

Estimating indicators at a variable-scale will greatly impact measurements:

-   Larger zones will likely have more species

-   Large areas are expected to contain more variation and rare occurrences (large size captures more unusual observations)

-   Variation BETWEEN observations over larger areas is typically less

    -   Measurments at larger scales (e.g. larger strata) lack the resolution to pick up smaller-scale variation, and measurements increasingly drift towards the "global-average"[^exploring-old-condition-data-2].

[^exploring-old-condition-data-2]: Known as "regression towards the mean"

![Comparing across variably-sized survey areas can be challenging: Observations over larger areas typically capture more variation and record measurments closer to the "global mean" with less variation between them. This is particuarlly obvious in the example here, where one site is split into different survey sizes, but the same effect exists in comparisons between different sites with diffferent survey sizes](images/quadrat%20size%20effect%202026-02-27%2010.41.53.excalidraw.png){width="907"}

## Caveat 4: Scaling up of indicator measurements, not indicator scores

> *We are not aiming to assess the condition of an imagined "average" area of woodland. We are assessing the condition of actual locations, then aggregating those measures to the wider woodland*

Our new WECA approach typically measures and scores[^exploring-old-condition-data-3] indicators at plots, and then averages those [scores]{.underline} across the survey-zone. This difference is important (averaging plot-level indicator value scores, rather than averaging their measurements then scoring that zone-wide average measurement). WECA aims to represent the ecological condition of actual real-life locations within a wood, not the condition of an imagined area of "average" woodland. The thought experiment below illustrates the potential implications of these different approaches for scoring one indicator.

[^exploring-old-condition-data-3]: using a value function

![](images/a%20thought%20experiment%20on%20aggregation%20of%20scores%20vs%20measurements%202025-04-17%2012.02.58.excalidraw.png)

## Caveat 5: Inconsistent data collection: missing data or implied absence

The data using the old method often includes blank or NULL values. Often, it is clear that this is inferred as an absence of the feature being measured (e.g. no deadwood present), here curation was carried out to determine where this could safely be assumed.

## Caveat 6: Impossible data

A notable number of impossible measurements were recorded (e.g. measurements of tree cover along with 0 tree species richness), curation attempted to rectify these and remove those data points, but they do speak to the challenges that are apparent in the data set relating to data recording and digitisation and the inconcistencies that can creep in through that process.

## Caveat 7: Use of DAFOR scale

The DAFOR scale was used to assess the combination of cover and abundance of indicators within a single score, with rough guidance attached that also suggested inconsistency was expected between indicators in the meaning of different DAFOR categories.

Notably, no 0 measurement was included, and so it is not always clear whether an absence implies a zero or represents a missing value.

| Class      | Cover guidance |
|------------|----------------|
| Dominant   | \>75% cover    |
| Abundant   | 51-75% cover   |
| Frequent   | 26-50% cover   |
| Occasional | 11-25% cover   |
| Rare       | 1-10% cover    |

## Caveat 8: Does DAFOR Rare mean absent??????!?!?!?!

```{r f_format_indicators}

# function to get all cols for an indicator ----
indicator_cols <- function(df, indicator) {
  grep(
    paste0("^", indicator, "_(?:Plot[0-9]+|Overall)$"),
    names(df),
    value = TRUE
  )
}

# function to format indicators ----
format_indicators <- function(df, indicator_types) {


  for (i in seq_len(nrow(indicator_types))) {
    ind  <- indicator_types$indicator[i]
    type <- indicator_types$type[i]
    cols <- indicator_cols(df, ind)

    if (length(cols) == 0) next
    if (type == "dafor") {
      df <- df %>%
        mutate(
          across(
            all_of(cols),
            ~ factor(.x, levels = dafor_levels, ordered = TRUE)
          )
        )} else if (type == "logical") {
          df <- df %>%
            mutate(across(all_of(cols), as.logical)
                   )
          } else if (type %in% c("numeric", "richness")) {
            df <- df %>%
              mutate(across(all_of(cols), as.numeric))
          }}
  df
}

```
```{r constants}
# Regex patterns to detect plot numbers and overall columns
plot_regex <- "(\\.|_)?[Pp]lot\\.?([0-9]+)$"  # matches variants like Plot1, plot.2, _plot3
overall_regex <- "\\.Overall$"                # matches columns ending in .Overall

```

```{r cnd_rename_cols}
# standardising plot/overall indicator nomeculature in col names ----
# Function to canonicalise a column name while keeping dots and adding Plot/Overall suffix
canonicalise_colname <- function(x) {

  # 1️⃣ Extract plot number (if any)
  plot_num <- str_extract(x, plot_regex)
  plot_num <- ifelse(is.na(plot_num), NA, str_extract(plot_num, "[0-9]+"))

  # 2️⃣ Detect Overall
  is_overall <- grepl(overall_regex, x)

  # 3️⃣ Strip Plot / Overall FIRST
  core <- x %>%
    gsub(plot_regex, "", ., ignore.case = TRUE) %>%   # remove Plot suffix
    gsub(overall_regex, "", ., ignore.case = TRUE)    # remove Overall suffix

  # 4️⃣ Canonicalise indicator naming on the *core*
  core <- core %>%
    gsub("NativesNumberPresent$", ".Native.richness", ., ignore.case = FALSE) %>%
    gsub("NonNativesNumberPresent$", ".Non.Native.richness", ., ignore.case = FALSE) %>%
    gsub("\\.Natives\\.Present$", ".Native.richness", ., ignore.case = FALSE) %>%
    gsub("\\.NonNatives\\.Present$", ".Non.Native.richness", ., ignore.case = FALSE) %>% 
    gsub("\\SSDAFOROfCover$", "Shrub.Cover", ., ignore.case = FALSE) %>% 
      # Fix cases like: 
          # RSSNon.Native.richness  -> RSS.Non.Native.richness
          # RSS.Non.Native.richness -> unchanged
    gsub("^([A-Z]{2,4})\\.?Non\\.", "\\1.Non.", .)


  # 5️⃣ Reattach Plot / Overall in a consistent way
  if (!is.na(plot_num)) {
    paste0(core, "_Plot", plot_num)
  } else if (is_overall) {
    paste0(core, "_Overall")
  } else {
    core
  }
}

old.names <- names(cnd)
names(cnd) <- names(cnd) %>% sapply(canonicalise_colname) %>% as.character()

# some more renaming

    TA.Intervention.Desirable = TAIntervention.Desirable,

  )
```

```{r cnd_standardise_missing_yesno}
missing_vals <- c("NULL", "null", " ", "N/A", "", "NA", "n/a", "Null", "N")
cnd <- cnd %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character),
                ~iconv(.x, from = "", to = "UTF-8", sub = " "))) %>% # 
  mutate(across(everything(), ~{
    x <- trimws(as.character(.))

    # Standardize missing values
    x[x %in% missing_vals] <- NA

    # yes/no → TRUE/FALSE
    x[tolower(x) == "yes"] <- TRUE
    x[tolower(x) == "no"]  <- FALSE

    # If column now only contains logical-like values, convert it
    if (all(x %in% c("TRUE", "FALSE", NA))) x <- as.logical(x)

    x
  }))

curation_notes_initial <- character()

curation_notes_initial <- c(
  curation_notes_initial,
  "\n### Initial curation\n",
  "- Standardised missing values (NULL, N/A, etc.) were converted yes/no to TRUE/FALSE",
  "- 'TemporaryPercentMax' (which relates to the upper bound of appropriate temporary open habtiat percentage) was missing in the original dataset, apparently replaced by a duplicate of OpenSpaceRidesPercentMax. This was renamed and filled with NA values (as the information was missing)."
  )
```

```{r lookup_indicator_types_format_theme}

## ID indicator names  ----
indicator_names <- names(cnd) %>%
  grep("_Overall$", ., value = TRUE) %>%
  sub("_Overall$", "", .)

## check entries at each indicator ---- 

indicator_freq_tables <- indicator_names %>%
  setNames(., .) %>%   # name the list by indicator
  lapply(function(ind) {

    # all columns for this indicator (plots + overall)
    cols <- names(cnd) %>%
      grep(paste0("^", ind, "_"), ., value = TRUE)

    # combine values across plots + overall
    values <- cnd %>%
      dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(cols)) %>%
      unlist(use.names = FALSE)

    # frequency table (including NA)
    table(values, useNA = "ifany")
  })

# initial check that no wild unexpected entries
# indicator_freq_tables 

## format indicator types ----

dafor_levels <- c("D", "A", "F", "O", "R", "Absent") %>% rev()# including "Absent" for missing data assumed as absence

is_numeric_chr <- function(x) {
  all(grepl("^[-+]?[0-9]*\\.?[0-9]+$", x))
}

is_logical_chr <- function(x) {
  all(x %in% c("TRUE", "FALSE"))
}

is_dafor_chr <- function(x, dafor_levels) {
  sum(x %in% dafor_levels) >= 3
}


indicator_types <- indicator_freq_tables %>%
  imap_dfr(function(tbl, indicator) {

    vals <- names(tbl)
    vals <- vals[!is.na(vals) & vals != "<NA>"]

    tibble(
      indicator    = indicator,
      n_unique     = length(vals),
      is_dafor     = is_dafor_chr(vals, dafor_levels),
      is_logical   = is_logical_chr(vals),
      is_numeric   = is_numeric_chr(vals)
    )
  }) %>%
  mutate(
    type = case_when(
      is_dafor   ~ "dafor",
      is_logical ~ "logical",
      is_numeric ~ "numeric",
      TRUE       ~ "unknown"
    )
  ) 

# group indicators by theme -----
indicator_types$theme <- NA_character_
indicator_types$theme[grep("^TA\\.", indicator_types$indicator)] <- "tree_age"
indicator_types$theme[grep("^(TS|SS)\\.", indicator_types$indicator)] <- "tree_shrub_species_richness"
indicator_types$theme[indicator_types$indicator %in% c("TS.Canopy.Dominated.By.One.Or.Two.SPP",
                                                       "SS.Shrub.Layer.Dominated.By.One.Or.Two.SPP") ] <- "tree_shrub_species_dominated"

indicator_types$theme[grep("Shrub.Cover", indicator_types$indicator)] <- "shrub_cover"
indicator_types$theme[grep("^(LTR|LSR)\\.", indicator_types$indicator)] <- "regeneration_level"
indicator_types$theme[grep("^(RTS|RSS)\\.", indicator_types$indicator)] <- "regeneration_species_richness"
indicator_types$theme[indicator_types$indicator %in% c("RTS.Dominated.By.One.Or.Two.SPP",
                                                       "RSS.Dominated.By.One.Or.Two.SPP") ] <- "regeneration_species_dominated"

indicator_types$theme[grep("^Flora\\.", indicator_types$indicator)] <- "flora"
indicator_types$theme[grep("^Deadwood\\.", indicator_types$indicator)] <- "deadwood"
indicator_types$theme[grep("^Invasives\\.", indicator_types$indicator)] <- "invasives"
indicator_types$theme[grep("^Animal\\.Damage\\.", indicator_types$indicator)] <- "animal_damage"
indicator_types$theme[grep("^Human\\.Impacts\\.", indicator_types$indicator)] <- "human_impact"
indicator_types$theme[grep("^Tree\\.Health\\.", indicator_types$indicator)] <- "tree_health"

indicator_types <- indicator_types %>% 
  arrange(theme)

```

```{r lookup_extended}

indicator <- indicator_types$indicator

# indicator group rules
indicator_group <- case_when(
  indicator %in% indicator_types$indicator[indicator_types$theme == "tree_age"] ~ "TA",
  indicator %in% indicator_types$indicator[indicator_types$theme == "shrub_cover"] ~ "SC",
  indicator %in% indicator_types$indicator[indicator_types$theme == "flora"] ~ "Flora",
  indicator %in% indicator_types$indicator[indicator_types$theme == "deadwood"] ~ "Deadwood",
  indicator %in% indicator_types$indicator[indicator_types$theme == "invasives"] ~ "Invasives",
  indicator %in% indicator_types$indicator[indicator_types$theme == "animal_damage"] ~ "Animal.Damage",
  indicator %in% indicator_types$indicator[indicator_types$theme == "human_impact"] ~ "Human.Impacts",
  indicator %in% indicator_types$indicator[indicator_types$theme == "tree_health"] ~ "Tree.Health",

  str_detect(indicator, "^LTR") ~ "LTR",
  str_detect(indicator, "^LSR") ~ "LSR",
  
  str_detect(indicator, "^TS") ~ "TS",
  str_detect(indicator, "^SS") ~ "SS",
  str_detect(indicator, "^RTS") ~ "RTS",
  str_detect(indicator, "^RSS") ~ "RSS",
  TRUE ~ NA_character_
)

# define group
group_col_map <- tibble(
  indicator_group = c(
    "TA", "SC", "Flora", "Deadwood", "Invasives",
    "Animal.Damage", "Human.Impacts", "Tree.Health",
    "LTR", "LSR", "TS", "SS", "RTS", "RSS"

    "TA", "SS", "Flora", "Deadwood", "Invasives",
    "Animal.Damage", "Human.Impact", "Tree.Health",
    "LTR", "LSR", "TS", "SS", "RTS", "RSS"
  )
)

# build lookup
indicator_lookup_extended <- tibble(
  indicator = indicator_types$indicator,
  indicator_group = indicator_group
) %>%
  left_join(group_col_map, by = "indicator_group") %>%
  mutate(
    notes_col = paste0(notes_prefix, ".NotesActions"),
    intervention_desirable_col = paste0(notes_prefix, ".Intervention.Desirable"),
    intervention_achievable_col = paste0(notes_prefix, ".Intervention.Achievable")
  ) %>%
  select(-notes_prefix)
```

```{r plot-level-data-extraction}

## want a survey tidy data frame with:
### id, Site.Name, ActualObservationDate, Key.Feature, Stratum, Plot.Number, measure for each indicator

# initial curation_notes_initial ----
long_plots  <- cnd %>%
  select(
    all_of(survey.info.cols),
    all_of(plot_cols)
  ) %>%
  # pivot longer to get col for indicator and plot number
  mutate(across(all_of(plot_cols), as.character)) %>% ## covert to character to ensure pivot works
  pivot_longer( # lengthen to get indicator and plot number cols
    cols = all_of(plot_cols),
    names_to = "indicator_plot",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  mutate( # use to create Plot.Number and indicator cols
    Plot.Number = str_extract(indicator_plot, "(?<=_Plot)\\d+") %>% as.integer(),
    indicator   = str_remove(indicator_plot, "_Plot\\d+$")
  ) %>%
  # select relevant cols to take forward
  select(
    all_of(survey.info.cols),
    Plot.Number,
    indicator,
    value
  ) %>%
  # widen to have one col per indicator
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = indicator,
    values_from = value
  ) %>%
  # drop all rows with NA throuhgout all cols with names in indicator_types$indicator
  filter(
    if_any(
      all_of(indicator_types$indicator),
      ~ !is.na(.x)
    )
  ) %>% 
  arrange(id, Plot.Number) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  format_indicators(., indicator_types)


curation_notes_initial <- c(
  curation_notes_initial,
  "- Plot-level and overall data were separated, with plot data converted into long format (row for each plot)\n\n"
  )

results$n.plots_og <- nrow(long_plots)  
results$n.plot_sites_og <- length(unique(long_plots$Site.Name))
```

```{r formatting}
# formating indicator types as in cnd ----
## Apply type formatting

# format each indicator coloum data type ----
for (i in seq_along(indicator_types$indicator)) {
  ind <- indicator_types$indicator[i]
  
  # look up the type for this indicator
  ind_type <- indicator_types$type[indicator_types$indicator == ind]
  
  # apply formatting to the entire column
  if (ind_type == "dafor") {
    long_plots[, ind] <- factor(
      long_plots[, ind],
      levels  = dafor_levels,   # e.g. c("A","D","F","O","R")
      ordered = TRUE
    )} else if (ind_type == "logical") {
      long_plots[, ind] <- as.logical(long_plots[, ind])
      } else if (ind_type %in% c("numeric", "richness")) {
        long_plots[, ind] <- as.numeric(long_plots[, ind])
        } else {
          # unknown type → leave unchanged
          long_plots[, ind] <- long_plots[, ind]
        }
}
```

# Deriving WECA-equivalent Values

```{r WECA-transcribe_setup}
#  transcribe to WECA-like indicators -----
# ...based on some intuitive thinking with MH, assuming 5 sampling plots
weca_faux_indicators <- data.frame(
  indicator = NA,
  plot_comparibility = NA,
  overall_comparibility = NA,
  useful_weca_alternative = NA,
  notes = NA
)

# converting overall DAFOR to expected proportion of plots with X present
overall_weighting_lookup <- c(
  "Absent" = 0,
  "R" = 0.2,
  "O" = 0.4,
  "F" = 0.7,
  "A" = 1,
  "D" = 1
)

```

Here follows an initial draft of a method to transcribe the data collected during historic woodland condition assessment to something comparable to the methods used to measure and value the new WECA indicators.

Each indicator's WECA-transcription methodolgy was scored in terms of the reliability (0-5 score, expert opinion of EMcH and MH) at plot and overall level.

## General approach

The approach for each indicator was one of the following (in order of priority):

1.  Derive measurements akin to those from the WECA process and apply those same value functions.
2.  Apply value scores based on available or derived measurements, based on the expert opinion of EMcH and MH referencing that indicator's value functions.
3.  Report some measurement or derived measurement that bared some relevance to the WECA indicator, without any attempt to apply an ecological value.
4.  Not report on the indicator

This was done at plot and overall level (note `r mean(1*overall$n_plots == 0)` % of surveys did not include plot-level info).

Where a WECA-analogous value was derivable at plot level, we took the mean across plots, to allow zone-level assessment and comparison with the valuation of overall-level measurements.

### Converting "overall"-level DAFOR to plot-presence rate

Importantly, the WECA value functions were developed for plot level, so that is where they are most appropriate to use. Our approach to scoring "overall"-level DAFOR of features relating to indicators assumed that each DAFOR related to an expected proportion of plot-level presence for that features at a rate of: Absent = 0, R = 0.2, O = 0.4, F = 0.7 and A/D = 1. Note caveats mentioned above, especially [Caveat 4: Scaling up of indicator measurements, not indicator scores].

-   Note this is very much non-ideal because it tells us nothing about the distribution of different features across plots e.g. for plot-level-presence of 0.5 for two different features, there is no way of knowing if 0.5 of plots have both, 0.5 have one and the other 0.5 the other, or anywhere in between those extremes. This is important because when the non-linear value functions are applied to measurements it will produce a very different average value if half of plots have 2 or 0, or if all have 1 of the features.

## Tree Age Structure

Plot-level comparability: 4.5

Overall-level comparability: 3

The WECA tree age structure indicator is based on the number of age classes present in each plot (maximum of 4: young, juvenile, Adult and mature). The old WCA data included DAFOR of five age classes trees (\< 20 years, 20-50 years, 50-100 years, 100-200 years and Veteran/Pollards/Ancient/Coppice Stools), which - while not directly comparable - are analogous.

1.  We combined the TA.Veteran.Pollards.Ancient.Coppice.Stools and TA.100.200.Years indicators to create a 'mature' category (max of their DAFOR).
2.  We counted the number of age classes present in plots.
3.  For "overall" data we assumed plot-level presence at a rate as described above ([Converting "overall"-level DAFOR to plot-presence rate]) and summed these across the age class indicators to give a score between 0 and 4.".
4.  The WECA value function was then applied to those 0-4 measurements.

```{r age_class_indicators_derivation}
## 7.1 age class indicators ----
# number of age classes present, combinign max(TA.Veteran.Pollards.Ancient.Coppice.Stools and TA.100.200.Years)

# does R mean absent???

long_plots$TA_mature <- pmax(long_plots$TA.Veteran.Pollards.Ancient.Coppice.Stools,
  long_plots$TA.100.200.Years, na.rm = TRUE
)
long_plots$TA_count <- row_sum_na_if_all_na(
  long_plots[, c( "TA.Less.Than.20.Years", "TA.20.50.Years", "TA.50.100.Years", "TA_mature")] > "Absent")

# aa = long_plots[,c("TA.Less.Than.20.Years", "TA.20.50.Years", "TA.50.100.Years", "TA.100.200.Years","TA.Veteran.Pollards.Ancient.Coppice.Stools", "TA_mature", "TA_count")]

# overall ----
overall$TA_mature <- pmax(overall$TA.Veteran.Pollards.Ancient.Coppice.Stools,
  overall$TA.100.200.Years, na.rm = TRUE
)
#cbind(overall$TA.Veteran.Pollards.Ancient.Coppice.Stools, overall$TA.100.200.Years, overall$TA_mature)
overall$TA_count <- row_sum_na_if_all_na(
  overall[, c( "TA.Less.Than.20.Years", "TA.20.50.Years", "TA.50.100.Years", "TA_mature")] %>% 
    mutate_all(~ overall_weighting_lookup[.]))

## valuing ---- 

long_plots$WECA_tree_age_score <- approx(
  x = age_lookup$N_ages,
  y = age_lookup$value,
  xout = long_plots$TA_count
)$y

plot_av_bysurvey_tree_age <- long_plots %>%
  group_by(id) %>%

    plot_av_n_tree_ages = mean(TA_count, na.rm = TRUE),
    plot_av_tree_age_score = mean(WECA_tree_age_score, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

overall$WECA_tree_age_score_overall <- approx(
  x = age_lookup$N_ages,
  y = age_lookup$value,
  xout = overall$TA_count
)$y

overall <- overall %>% 
  left_join(plot_av_bysurvey_tree_age, by = "id")                
# cbind(overall$TA_count, overall$WECA_tree_age_score_overall, overall$plot_av_n_tree_ages, overall$plot_av_tree_age_score)  
                                                                
                                                                  
weca_faux_indicators <- weca_faux_indicators %>%
```

## Canopy nativness

Plot-level comparability: 1

Overall-level comparability: 0.5

WECA canopy nativness is based on the percentage volume of the tree and shrub canopy that is UK-native. The closest measurements in the old WCA data was native and non-native species richness for both tree and shrub species separately. Here, we report those species richness measurements, and use them to determine if the canopy is entirely native, or entirely non-native or mixed (unable to give any higher precision), we made no attempt here to value this indicator ecologically.

We can be confident about the extremities (all native or all non-native), but valuing mixed canopies was deemed unreliable.

Note [Caveat 3: Varying plot and zone size affect indicator measurements]: larger plots/zones are more likely to be mixed, purely because of their larger sampling area being more likely to pick up different species.

```{r canopy_nativness}
## 7.2 canopy nativness ----
## TS.Native.richness, TS.Non.Native.richness, TS.Canopy.Dominated.By.One.Or.Two.SPP, SS.Native.richness, SS.Non.Native.richness, SS.Shrub.Layer.Dominated.By.One.Or.Two.SPP

# where only native/ non native can be sure
# where shrub is one and tree species another???
# cant graduate
sum_na_if_all_na <- function(x) {
  out <- rowSums(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  out[rowSums(!is.na(x)) == 0] <- NA
  out
}

long_plots$N_native_treeshrub <- sum_na_if_all_na(cbind(long_plots$TS.Native.richness,
                                                        long_plots$SS.Native.richness))

long_plots$N_nonnative_treeshrub <- sum_na_if_all_na(cbind(long_plots$TS.Non.Native.richness,
                                                           long_plots$SS.Non.Native.richness))

overall$N_native_treeshrub <- sum_na_if_all_na(cbind(overall$TS.Native.richness,
                                                     overall$SS.Native.richness))

overall$N_nonnative_treeshrub <- sum_na_if_all_na(cbind(overall$TS.Non.Native.richness,
                                                        overall$SS.Non.Native.richness))

long_plots$canopy_all_native <- ifelse(
  long_plots$N_nonnative_treeshrub == 0 & long_plots$N_native_treeshrub > 0 ,
  TRUE, NA)
long_plots$canopy_all_nonnative <- ifelse(
  long_plots$N_nonnative_treeshrub > 0 & long_plots$N_native_treeshrub == 0 ,
  TRUE, NA)
long_plots$canopy_mixed <- ifelse(
  long_plots$N_nonnative_treeshrub > 0 & long_plots$N_native_treeshrub > 0,
  TRUE, NA)
long_plots$canopy_makeup <- case_when(
  long_plots$canopy_all_native ~ "All native",
  long_plots$canopy_all_nonnative ~ "All non-native",
  long_plots$canopy_mixed ~ "Mixed",
  TRUE ~ NA_character_
)

overall$canopy_all_native <- ifelse(
  (overall$N_nonnative_treeshrub == 0 & overall$N_native_treeshrub > 0 ),
  TRUE, NA)
overall$canopy_all_nonnative <- ifelse(
  (overall$N_nonnative_treeshrub > 0 & overall$N_native_treeshrub == 0 ),
  TRUE, NA)
overall$canopy_mixed <- ifelse(
  (overall$N_nonnative_treeshrub > 0 & overall$N_native_treeshrub > 0),
  TRUE, NA)
overall$canopy_makeup <- case_when(
  overall$canopy_all_native ~ "All native",
  overall$canopy_all_nonnative ~ "All non-native",
  overall$canopy_mixed ~ "Mixed",
  TRUE ~ NA_character_
)
                                     


weca_faux_indicators <- weca_faux_indicators %>%
  add_row(
    indicator = "Canopy nativness",
    plot_comparibility = 1,
    overall_comparibility = 0.5,
    useful_weca_alternative = NA,
    notes = "Extremes (all native or all non-native) are comparable, but mixed canopy is not.")


```

## Vertical structure

Plot-level comparability: 2

Overall-level comparability: 1

WECA vertical structure is based on the number of vegetation layers with \>10% vegetation cover in plots (six layers: ground, field, shrub, canopy low, mid & high). The old WCA data did not have directly comparable data, but did have some measurements that related to vegetation at the lower three vertical layers that we used to create some indicators with some degree of indirect comparability. Importantly, the lowest two strata needed to be combined (ground/field, shrub) and any comparison would only be possible with the lower-canopy levels from the new WECA data, and even then, with the caveat that the strata are indirect estimates.

-   Ground and field layer (inseparable):

    -   DAFOR of different ground flora classes, seedlings and saplings of trees and shrubs

-   Shrub layer: DAFOR max of shrub cover and trees \< 20 years

-   Canopy layers (not possible): tree age class DAFOR were deemed inappropriate for defining vertical stratification.

A score to aproximpate the number of the three lower strata with ecologically functioning vegetation structure (DAFOR score \>= O) was calculated by summing scores (notably allowing for half-presences):

-   Shrub layer (1): Shrub cover

-   Ground flora (1): max( Flora.Ancient.Woodland.Plants..Specialists., Flora.Other.Woodland.Plants..Generalists., Flora.Other.Native.Plants, Flora.Coarse.Vegetation, Flora.Other.Plants)

-   Seedlings (0.5): max(LTR.Seedlings.Less.Than.10cm, LTR.Seedlings.10.100cm, LSR.Seedlings.Less.Than.10cm, LSR.Seedlings.10.100cm)

-   Saplings (0.5): max (LTR.Saplings.Greater.Than.100cm, LSR.Saplings.Greater.Than.100cm)

The overall level further weighted each score indicator by the assumed plot-level presence rate (see [Converting "overall"-level DAFOR to plot-presence rate]).

No attempt was made here to value this indicator. Any comparison to the new WECA should be based on comparision to those lower three layers."

Note [Caveat 3: Varying plot and zone size affect indicator measurements]: larger plots/zones are more likely to have more vertical layers simply because of their larger sampling area.

```{r verticle_structure}
## 7.3 verticle structure ----

# WECA
## count of 0-6
## only where >DOMIN 5 10% cover of plot

# considering only occational or greater (>11%) at plot level

# ground layer <0.1  or field layer ----
# Flora.Ancient.Woodland.Plants..Specialists., Flora.Other.Woodland.Plants..Generalists., Flora.Other.Native.Plants, Flora.Coarse.Vegetation, Flora.Other.Plants, Flora.No.Vegitation
# LTR.Seedlings.Less.Than.10cm, LTR.Saplings.Greater.Than.100cm, LTR.Coppice.Regrowth.or.Suckering
# LSR.Seedlings.Less.Than.10cm, LSR.Saplings.Greater.Than.100cm, 

long_plots$ground_flora <- pmax(
  long_plots$Flora.Ancient.Woodland.Plants..Specialists.,
  long_plots$Flora.Other.Woodland.Plants..Generalists.,
  long_plots$Flora.Other.Native.Plants,
  long_plots$Flora.Coarse.Vegetation,
  long_plots$Flora.Other.Plants,
  na.rm = TRUE
)
overall$ground_flora <- pmax(
  overall$Flora.Ancient.Woodland.Plants..Specialists.,
  overall$Flora.Other.Woodland.Plants..Generalists.,
  overall$Flora.Other.Native.Plants,
  overall$Flora.Coarse.Vegetation,
  overall$Flora.Other.Plants,
  na.rm = TRUE
)


long_plots$seedlings <- pmax(
  long_plots$LTR.Seedlings.Less.Than.10cm,
  long_plots$LTR.Seedlings.10.100cm,
  long_plots$LSR.Seedlings.Less.Than.10cm,
  long_plots$LSR.Seedlings.10.100cm,
  na.rm = TRUE
)
overall$seedlings <- pmax(
  overall$LTR.Seedlings.Less.Than.10cm,
  overall$LTR.Seedlings.10.100cm,
  overall$LSR.Seedlings.Less.Than.10cm,
  overall$LSR.Seedlings.10.100cm,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

long_plots$saplings <- pmax(
  long_plots$LTR.Saplings.Greater.Than.100cm,
  long_plots$LSR.Saplings.Greater.Than.100cm,
  na.rm = TRUE
)
overall$saplings <- pmax(
  overall$LTR.Saplings.Greater.Than.100cm,
  overall$LSR.Saplings.Greater.Than.100cm,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

# shrub layer ----
# Shrub.Cover

long_plots$shrub_layer <- pmax(
  long_plots$Shrub.Cover,
  long_plots$TA.Less.Than.20.Years,
  na.rm = TRUE
)
overall$shrub_layer <- pmax(
  overall$Shrub.Cover,
  overall$TA.Less.Than.20.Years,
  na.rm = TRUE
)


# Alt measurement out of 3 ----

long_plots$verticle_structure_N <- row_sum_na_if_all_na(
  cbind(1*(long_plots$ground_flora > "O"),
        0.5*(long_plots$seedlings > "O"),
        0.5*(long_plots$saplings > "O"),
        1*(long_plots$shrub_layer > "O")))

plot_av_bysurvey_verticle_structure <- long_plots %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(
    plot_av_verticle_structure_N = mean(verticle_structure_N, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# overall weigthed by aupssumed plot-level presence (R = 0.2, O = 0.4, F = 0.7, A/D = 1)
overall$verticle_structure_N_overall <- row_sum_na_if_all_na(
  cbind(1*(overall_weighting_lookup[overall$ground_flora] %>% as.numeric()),
        0.5*(overall_weighting_lookup[overall$seedlings] %>% as.numeric()),
        0.5*(overall_weighting_lookup[overall$saplings] %>% as.numeric()),
        1*(overall_weighting_lookup[overall$shrub_layer] %>% as.numeric())))
overall <- overall %>%
  left_join(plot_av_bysurvey_verticle_structure, by = "id")
  

# poss alt WECA indicator for comparison combining these three layers (with one combined)

# plot level 2
# overall 1

```

This plot explores the lower layers measurement: plot-level average and overall level measurement. 

- Notably, there are many 0 measurements at the overall level, this could be an artifact from the curation process, where absence was assumed incorrectly, regardless, it casts some doubt on the reliability of those overall-level measures of this indicator. It might be worth removing those from further analysis (accepting that this will fail to represent those surveys that in truth had no lower canopy layers)

## Tree and Shrub - Appropriate species

Plot-level comparability: 3

Overall-level comparability: 2

WECA recorded all tree and shrub species present in plots and calculated the proportion of species present (young or older) from a list of appropriate species for that habitat type (of six habitat types). The old WCA recorded the number of native tree and the number of native shrub species and did not record habitat type in a way comparable to WECA.

Here we:

1.  Summed the number of native tree and shrub species at plot and overall levels
2.  Calculated the region-specific 80th percentile of native tree and shrub SR, and used that as the "expected native SR", for plots and overall separately.
3.  Calculated the proportion of "expected native SR" present in each plot and overall survey (truncated to a ceiling of 1).
4.  Transformed the value function for tree and shrub species richness so that it maxed out at 100 where "proportion of expected native SR" was 1.
5.  Applied the transformed value function

Note, this is really a different value function, but transfers some of the "spirit" of the WECA value function approach. It might be worth experimenting with different percentiles for better comparison, once WECA data starts coming in and/or create an alternative WECA indicator for legacy comparison purposes.

```{r species-approprite}
## 7.4 native species richness ------

# trust site managers to know nativnes
# take regional 90th of all in regoin for denominator, calc proportion of that and hold that up to the value function

# TS.Native.richness, SS.Native.richness
# N_native_treeshrub derived above in canopy nativness section


# regional percentiles ----
plot_regional_90th_native_sr_trees_shrubs <- long_plots %>% 
  group_by(Region) %>%
  summarise(
    regional_90th_native_sr_trees_shrubs = quantile(N_native_treeshrub, 0.9, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
overall_regional_90th_native_sr_trees_shrubs <- overall %>%
  group_by(Region) %>%
  summarise(
    regional_90th_native_sr_trees_shrubs = quantile(N_native_treeshrub, 0.9, na.rm = TRUE)
    )

# prop of regional 90th present ----
long_plots$prop_native_sr_trees_shrubs <- long_plots$N_native_treeshrub / 
  overall_regional_90th_native_sr_trees_shrubs$regional_90th_native_sr_trees_shrubs[match(long_plots$Region, overall_regional_90th_native_sr_trees_shrubs$Region)]
long_plots$prop_native_sr_trees_shrubs[long_plots$prop_native_sr_trees_shrubs>1] <- 1
overall$prop_native_sr_trees_shrubs <- overall$N_native_treeshrub / 
  overall_regional_90th_native_sr_trees_shrubs$regional_90th_native_sr_trees_shrubs[match(overall$Region, overall_regional_90th_native_sr_trees_shrubs$Region)]
overall$prop_native_sr_trees_shrubs[overall$prop_native_sr_trees_shrubs>1] <- 1

# valuation ----
# transform value function to be 0 - 1

tree_spp_lookup$per_spp <- tree_spp_lookup$per_spp - min(tree_spp_lookup$per_spp)
tree_spp_lookup$per_spp <- tree_spp_lookup$per_spp / max(tree_spp_lookup$per_spp)

long_plots$WECA_tree_shrub_sr_value_plot <- approx(
  x = tree_spp_lookup$per_spp,
  y = tree_spp_lookup$value,
  xout = long_plots$prop_native_sr_trees_shrubs
)$y

overall$WECA_tree_shrub_sr_value_overall <- approx(
  x = tree_spp_lookup$per_spp,
  y = tree_spp_lookup$value,
  xout = overall$prop_native_sr_trees_shrubs
)$y

# av and max plot value ----
plot_av.max_prop_native_sr_trees_shrubs <- long_plots %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(
    plotmax_prop_native_sr_trees_shrubs = max(prop_native_sr_trees_shrubs, na.rm = TRUE),
    plotav_prop_native_sr_trees_shrubs = mean(prop_native_sr_trees_shrubs, na.rm = TRUE),
    WECA_tree_shrub_sr_value_plot_av = mean(WECA_tree_shrub_sr_value_plot, na.rm = TRUE),
    ) %>% 
  select(id, plotmax_prop_native_sr_trees_shrubs, plotav_prop_native_sr_trees_shrubs, WECA_tree_shrub_sr_value_plot_av) %>% 
  # if inf og -inf make NA
  mutate(
    plotmax_prop_native_sr_trees_shrubs = ifelse(is.infinite(plotmax_prop_native_sr_trees_shrubs), NA, plotmax_prop_native_sr_trees_shrubs),
    plotav_prop_native_sr_trees_shrubs = ifelse(is.infinite(plotav_prop_native_sr_trees_shrubs), NA, plotav_prop_native_sr_trees_shrubs)
  )
overall <- overall %>%
  left_join(plot_av.max_prop_native_sr_trees_shrubs, by = "id")


# could compare to alt WECA summing species over site

# plot score 3
# overall score 2

```

## Invasives

Plot-level comparability: 3.5

Overall-level comparability: 2

WECA records the cover of individual invasive species and cover of all invasives combined within plots, value is 0 if any species classed as "high threat" are present, or otherwise assigned based on combined cover of invasives. The WCA data contains DAFOR cover estimates for Rhododendron, Himalayan balsam, Japanese knot-weed, giant hogweed and "other invasives". Those named species are all on the "high threat" list, but it also contains more species not recorded in WCA.

Here we:

1.  Assigned a value of 0 to plots with a named invasive present.
2.  Assigned value to plots with no named invasives based on DAFOR of "other invasives" , referencing the WECA value function (D or A = 0; F = 10; O = 33; R = 70; Absent = 100)
3.  Assigned an "initial value" to overall surveys based on plot-presence rate derived from DAFOR of named invasives (see [Converting "overall"-level DAFOR to plot-presence rate].
4.  Multiplied overall-level "initial value" by a factor based on DAFOR of "other invasives" (as above for plot level)

```{r invasives}
## 7.5 invasives ------
#caveat some high therat not on list
# confidence score:
## plot score 3.5
## overall 2


# high threat = Invasives.Rhododendron, Invasives.Himalayan.Balsam, Invasives.Japanese.Knotweed, Invasives.Giant.Hogweed, 
# other = Invasives.Other

# high threat at plot = 0 score
long_plots$high_threat_invasive <- pmax(
  long_plots$Invasives.Rhododendron,
  long_plots$Invasives.Himalayan.Balsam,
  long_plots$Invasives.Japanese.Knotweed,
  na.rm = TRUE
)
overall$high_threat_invasive <- pmax(
  overall$Invasives.Rhododendron,
  overall$Invasives.Himalayan.Balsam,
  overall$Invasives.Japanese.Knotweed,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

# only other, value  R = 0.7  , O = 0.33ish  F = 0.10, A = 0

long_plots$invasive_value_other <- case_when(
  long_plots$Invasives.Other == "Absent" ~ 1,
  long_plots$Invasives.Other == "R" ~ 0.7,
  long_plots$Invasives.Other == "O" ~ 0.33,
  long_plots$Invasives.Other == "F" ~ 0.1,
  long_plots$Invasives.Other %in% c("A", "D") ~ 0
)
overall$invasive_value_other <- case_when(
  overall$Invasives.Other == "Absent" ~ 1,
  overall$Invasives.Other == "R" ~ 0.7,
  overall$Invasives.Other == "O" ~ 0.33,
  overall$Invasives.Other == "F" ~ 0.1,
  overall$Invasives.Other %in% c("A", "D") ~ 0
)

long_plots$invasive_value_high_threat_multiplier <- ifelse(long_plots$high_threat_invasive > "Absent", 0, 1)

# hi threat at overall
# R = 0.8
# O = 0.6
# F = 0.2 
# D-A = 0
# 1*(overall_weighting_lookup[overall$high_threat_invasive] %>% as.numeric())

overall$invasive_value_high_threat_multiplier <- 1-(1*(overall_weighting_lookup[overall$high_threat_invasive] %>% as.numeric()))

long_plots$WECA_invasive_score <- long_plots$invasive_value_other * long_plots$invasive_value_high_threat_multiplier

overall$WECA_invasive_score <- overall$invasive_value_other * overall$invasive_value_high_threat_multiplier

plot_ave_bysurvey_invasives <- long_plots %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(
    plot_av_invasive_score = mean(WECA_invasive_score, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
overall <- overall %>%
  left_join(plot_ave_bysurvey_invasives, by = "id")
```

## Deadwood

Plot-level comparability: 2

Overall-level comparability: 1

WECA records the presence of four different deadwood types in each plot-quarter (lying, standing, in-canopy and stumps), and sums these (max 16). The WCA data recorded DAFOR of deadwood standing and fallen, separately.

Here we:

1.  Assumed that standing and fallen deadwood categories from WCA were analogous to the standing and lying WECA categories, respectively.
2.  Assumed that plot-level DAFOR related to plot-quarter presences (D = 4; A = 2; F or O = 1; R or Absent = 0)
3.  Summed the plot-quarter-deadwood-types at plot level (max 8)
4.  Calculated the max cover of standing and lying deadwood at "overall"-level, for comparison and reporting across WCA surveys.

Valuation of the plot-level measurements was not attempted yet, this may be possible by e.g. exploring WECA data to calibrate the expected WECA score based solely on lying and standing deadwood. It will also be possible to use this analog indicator to track change in a subset of the WECA deadwood data (i.e. standing and lying deadwood only)

No attempt is made to value the WCA overall-level deadwood cover estimates, we simply report the cover of standing and fallen deadwood, and their maximum.

```{r deadwood}
## 7.6 deadwood ------
# only two types - Deadwood.Standing, Deadwood.Fallen
## could compare to the standing and fallen parts of WECA 
## shoudl really calobrate /16 score rather than assume constancy between deadwood type accumulation and value
# confidence score:
## plot score 2
## overall score 1


# plot level, number of quarters assumed
# D = 4
# A = 2
# O & F = 1
#  R = 0
long_plots$deadwood_score_standing <- case_when(
  long_plots$Deadwood.Standing == "Absent" ~ 0,
  long_plots$Deadwood.Standing == "R" ~ 0,
  long_plots$Deadwood.Standing == "O" ~ 1,
  long_plots$Deadwood.Standing == "F" ~ 1,
  long_plots$Deadwood.Standing == "A" ~ 2,
  long_plots$Deadwood.Standing == "D" ~ 4
)
long_plots$deadwood_score_fallen <- case_when(
  long_plots$Deadwood.Fallen == "Absent" ~ 0,
  long_plots$Deadwood.Fallen == "R" ~ 0,
  long_plots$Deadwood.Fallen == "O" ~ 1,
  long_plots$Deadwood.Fallen == "F" ~ 1,
  long_plots$Deadwood.Fallen == "A" ~ 2,
  long_plots$Deadwood.Fallen == "D" ~ 4
)
long_plots$deadwood_score_both <- row_sum_na_if_all_na(
  cbind(
    long_plots$deadwood_score_standing,
    long_plots$deadwood_score_fallen
  )
)

# overall
overall$deadwood_max <- pmax(
  overall$Deadwood.Standing,
  overall$Deadwood.Fallen,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

plot_av_bysurvey_deadwood_score_both <- long_plots %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(
    plot_av_deadwood_score = mean(deadwood_score_both, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
overall <- overall %>%
  left_join(plot_av_bysurvey_deadwood_score_both, by = "id")
```

## AVTs

Plot-level comparability: NA

Overall-level comparability: 3

WECA records the number of AVTs within 10 m of a 100m long transect from plots, uses that to estimate AVT density at each plot, and subsequently average density across the zone which is then valued using the value function. The WCA data includes DAFOR cover of "Veteran.Pollards.Ancient.Coppice.Stools". 

Here, we took the DAFOR of "Veteran.Pollards.Ancient.Coppice.Stools" at overall level and valued it, referring to the value function (D = 100; A = 75; F = 50; O = 25; R = 10; Absent = 0)

```{r AVTs}

  overall$TA.Veteran.Pollards.Ancient.Coppice.Stools == "R" ~ 10,

  overall$TA.Veteran.Pollards.Ancient.Coppice.Stools == "F" ~ 50,
  overall$TA.Veteran.Pollards.Ancient.Coppice.Stools == "A" ~ 75,
  overall$TA.Veteran.Pollards.Ancient.Coppice.Stools == "D" ~ 1
)

# overall score - 3
```

## Regeneration

Plot-level comparability: 5

Overall-level comparability: 3

Both WECA and the WCA record the cover of the same regen classes: seedlings, saplings and young trees. The WCA records these separately for trees and shrubs, and also splits saplings into two classes (\< 10 cm and 10 - 100 cm).

Here we:

1.  Took the max cover of all seedling regneration and all sapling regeneration, separately, at plot and "overall"-levels.
2.  Summed the number of regeneration classes present in each plot
3.  Converted the cover of each class at "overall"-level to a plot-presence rate (see [Converting "overall"-level DAFOR to plot-presence rate]) and summed these.
4.  Valued the regen class number using the (interpolated) value function

```{r regenetation}
## 7.8 regeneration ------
# LTR.Seedlings.Less.Than.10cm, LTR.Seedlings.10.100cm, LTR.Saplings.Greater.Than.100cm, 
# LSR.Seedlings.Less.Than.10cm, LSR.Seedlings.10.100cm, LSR.Saplings.Greater.Than.100cm, 
# TA young
# max 
# plot score 5
# overall score 3


long_plots$seedlings <- pmax(
  long_plots$LTR.Seedlings.Less.Than.10cm,
  long_plots$LTR.Seedlings.10.100cm,
  long_plots$LSR.Seedlings.Less.Than.10cm,
  long_plots$LSR.Seedlings.10.100cm,
  na.rm = TRUE
)
overall$seedlings <- pmax(
  overall$LTR.Seedlings.Less.Than.10cm,
  overall$LTR.Seedlings.10.100cm,
  overall$LSR.Seedlings.Less.Than.10cm,
  overall$LSR.Seedlings.10.100cm,
  na.rm = TRUE
)
long_plots$saplings <- pmax(
  long_plots$LTR.Saplings.Greater.Than.100cm,
  long_plots$LSR.Saplings.Greater.Than.100cm,
  na.rm = TRUE
)
overall$saplings <- pmax(
  overall$LTR.Saplings.Greater.Than.100cm,
  overall$LSR.Saplings.Greater.Than.100cm,
  na.rm = TRUE
)
long_plots$TA_young <- long_plots$TA.Less.Than.20.Years
overall$TA_young <- overall$TA.Less.Than.20.Years

long_plots$regeneration_score <- row_sum_na_if_all_na(
  cbind(1*(long_plots$seedlings > "Absent"),
        1*(long_plots$saplings > "Absent"),
        1*(long_plots$TA_young > "Absent")))
  
overall$regeneration_score <- row_sum_na_if_all_na(
  cbind(1*(overall_weighting_lookup[overall$seedlings] %>% as.numeric()),
        1*(overall_weighting_lookup[overall$saplings] %>% as.numeric()),
        1*(overall_weighting_lookup[overall$TA_young] %>% as.numeric()))
)

# value regeneration score using value function - 

long_plots$WECA_regen_value_plot <- approx(
  x = regen_lookup$N.Regen.classes.present,
  y = regen_lookup$value,
  xout = long_plots$regeneration_score
)$y

overall$WECA_regen_value_overall <- approx(
  x = regen_lookup$N.Regen.classes.present,
  y = regen_lookup$value,
  xout = overall$regeneration_score
)$y

plot_av.bysurvey_regeneration <- long_plots %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(
    plot_av_regeneration_N_classes_present = mean(regeneration_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    WECA_regen_value_plot_av = mean(WECA_regen_value_plot, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
overall <- overall %>%
  left_join(plot_av.bysurvey_regeneration, by = "id")

```

There was missing regeneration value for:
- `r mean(is.na(long_plots$WECA_regen_value_plot))*100` % of plots 
- `r mean(is.na(overall$WECA_regen_value_overall))*100` % of survey overall
- `r mean(is.na(overall$WECA_regen_value_plot_av))*100` % of survey plot-averages

### Plot of regeneration score, comparing mean of plots to overall.

Generally, the plot-average regeneration score is higher than the overall score
- probably partly due to the plot-rate-presence calculation.
- The non-representative nature of plots likely to also play a role.

The large number of 0 Overall score (particularly where plot-average is high) is worrying, these data may be best removed from further analysis.

## Herbivore impact

Plot-level comparability: 1.5

Overall-level comparability: 1

The WECA estimates herbivory level using a method akin to an ultra-lite Woodland Herbivore Impact Assessment[^exploring-old-condition-data-4]. The WCA gives a DAFOR for evidence of deer and "other animal" damage. 

We made not attempt to value these and simply reported the max animal damage DAFOR.

[^exploring-old-condition-data-4]: <https://www.forestry.gov.scot/publications/woodland-herbivore-impact-assessment-method-user-guide>

```{r herbivory}

# HIA survey info
```

## Tree health

Plot-level comparability: 2

Overall-level comparability: 1.5

WECA records the presence of priority pests and diseases and estimates the % basal area of rapid morality and crown dieback. Where priority pests and diseases are present a value of 0 is given, otherwise value is assigned based on the maximum of crown dieback or rapid tree mortality. WCA reported a DAFOR cover value of notifiable pest and disease and of "other" pest or disease. Notably "priority pests and diseases" and "notifiable pest and diseases" are not the same.

Similar to [Invasives], we:

1.  Assigned plot values of 0 where a notifiable pest or disease was present
2.  Assigned value to plots with no notifiable pest and diseases based on DAFOR of "other pests and diseases" , referencing the WECA value function (D or A = 0; F = 25; O = 50; R = 75; Absent = 100)
3.  Assigned an "initial value" to overall surveys based on plot-presence rate derived from DAFOR of notifiable pests and diseases (see [Converting "overall"-level DAFOR to plot-presence rate].
4.  Multiplied overall-level "initial value" by a factor based on DAFOR of "other pests and diseases" (as above for plot level)

```{r tree_health}
## 7.10 tree health ------
# Tree.Health.Notifiable.Pest.Or.Disease Tree.Health.Other.Disease.Or.Pest

# plot
# Tree.Health.Notifiable.Pest.Or.Disease present = 0
# Tree.Health.Other.Disease.Or.Pest DAF = 0, O = 10, R = 0.75

long_plots$tree_health_notifiable_multiplier <- ifelse(long_plots$Tree.Health.Notifiable.Pest.Or.Disease == "Absent", 1, 0)
long_plots$tree_health_other_multiplier <- case_when(
  long_plots$Tree.Health.Other.Disease.Or.Pest == "Absent" ~ 100,
  long_plots$Tree.Health.Other.Disease.Or.Pest == "R" ~ 75,
  long_plots$Tree.Health.Other.Disease.Or.Pest == "O" ~ 50,
  long_plots$Tree.Health.Other.Disease.Or.Pest == "F" ~ 25,
  long_plots$Tree.Health.Other.Disease.Or.Pest %in% c("A", "D") ~ 0
)
long_plots$WECA_tree_health_value <- long_plots$tree_health_notifiable_multiplier * long_plots$tree_health_other_multiplier

# overall
## same logic as high threat invasive
overall$tree_health_notifiable_multiplier <- 1-(1*(overall_weighting_lookup[overall$Tree.Health.Notifiable.Pest.Or.Disease] %>% as.numeric()))
  
overall$tree_health_other_multiplier <- case_when(
  overall$Tree.Health.Other.Disease.Or.Pest == "Absent" ~ 100,
  overall$Tree.Health.Other.Disease.Or.Pest == "R" ~ 75,
  overall$Tree.Health.Other.Disease.Or.Pest == "O" ~ 50,
  overall$Tree.Health.Other.Disease.Or.Pest == "F" ~ 25,
  overall$Tree.Health.Other.Disease.Or.Pest %in% c("A", "D") ~ 0
)
overall$WECA_tree_health_value_overall <- overall$tree_health_notifiable_multiplier * overall$tree_health_other_multiplier

plot_av_bysurvey_tree_health <- long_plots %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(
    WECA_tree_health_value_plot_av = mean(WECA_tree_health_value, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
overall <- overall %>%
  # if WECA_tree_health_value_plot_av exists, remove it
  select(-any_of("WECA_tree_health_value_plot_av")) %>%
  left_join(plot_av_bysurvey_tree_health, by = "id")


# plot score 2
# overall score 1.5



```


Plot of tree health value, comparing mean of plots to overall.

```{r plot_tree_health_score_plot_av_overall}
x_mean <- mean(overall$WECA_tree_health_value_plot_av, na.rm = TRUE)
y_mean <- mean(overall$WECA_tree_health_value_overall, na.rm = TRUE)

p <- ggplot(overall, aes(x = WECA_tree_health_value_plot_av, 
                         y = WECA_tree_health_value_overall,
               color = sr_changed_in_curation)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 1, height = 1, alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
       title = "Tree health score",
       x = "Average plot-level score",
       y = "Overall score",
       color = "SR changed in curation") +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = x_mean, linetype = "dotted") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = y_mean, linetype = "dotted") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

figure_plots$tree_health_score_plot_av_overall <- ggMarginal(
  p,
  type = "histogram",
  bins = 20,
  fill = "grey80",
  col = "white"
)
figure_plots$tree_health_score_plot_av_overall
```

## Ground Flora

Plot-level comparability: 0

Overall-level comparability: 0

WECA assesses the presence of ground flora within plots at the species level, determines the proportion of presence from a list of appropriate species specific to one of six habitat types, and uses the value function to score that "proportion of appropriate species present". WCA gave a DAFOR estimate for ancient woodland specialists plants, woodland generalist plants, other native plants, coarse vegetation, other plants and "no vegetation". These were deemed incomparable and no attempt was made to value them.


## Horizontal complexity

Plot-level comparability: 0

Overall-level comparability: 1

WECA assesses top height every 10m along a 100 m transect from plots and values the number of different top height classes recorded. The WCA has no real comparable data, accepting that it does report the percentage cover of tree canopy, shrub canopy, semi natural open space, rides and temporary open space. 

No attempt was made to value these.

We calculated a diversity score from the percentage covers of:
- tree canopy
- shrub canopy
- semi natural open space + rides + temporary open space + water

This metric should give some indication of relative horizontal complexity, but is not directly relatable to WECA

```{r horizontal_complexity}
## 7.12 Horizontal complexity ------
# only at overall level
## TotalTreeCanopyCoverPercentCurrent 
## OpenSpaceSemiNaturalHabitatPercentCurrent OpenSpaceRidesPercentCurrent OpenSpaceTemporaryPercentCurrent OpenSpaceWaterFeaturesPercentCurrent
## ShrubCoverPercentCurrent
# plot score 0
# overall score 1

overall$open_cover <- row_sum_na_if_all_na(
  overall %>% select(
     OpenSpaceSemiNaturalHabitatPercentCurrent,
     OpenSpaceRidesPercentCurrent,
     OpenSpaceTemporaryPercentCurrent,
     OpenSpaceWaterFeaturesPercentCurrent) %>% 
    #make numeric
    mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)))

# shannon diversity of cover types
overall <- overall %>%
  mutate(
    horizontal_complexity_alt_shannon = select(.,
      TotalTreeCanopyCoverPercentCurrent,
      ShrubCoverPercentCurrent,
      open_cover
    ) %>%
      mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) %>%
      apply(1, function(x) {
        
        p <- x / sum(x, na.rm = TRUE)
        p <- p[p > 0]
        
        -sum(p * log(p))
        
      })
    
  )

```

Histogram of horizontal complexity (Shannon diversity of cover types) at overall level.

```{r histogram_horizontal_complexity}
mean_horizontal_complexity <- mean(overall$horizontal_complexity_alt_shannon, na.rm =
  TRUE)
ggplot(overall, aes(x = horizontal_complexity_alt_shannon)) +
  
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 0.5,
    boundary = 0,
    fill = "grey80",
    colour = "white"
  ) +
  
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = mean_horizontal_complexity,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Overall-level horizontal complexity (Shannon diversity of cover types)",
    x = "Horizontal complexity",
    y = "Number of survey areas"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal()
```
## Human impact

Plot-level comparability: 2

Overall-level comparability: 1.5

WECA assesses the cover of human damage within plots and values that. WCA assesses the DAFOR cover of one off and continuous impacts.

Here we:

1.  Took the max of one off and continuous impacts
2.  Valued that at plot and overall level, with reference to the value function

```{r human_impact}
## 7.13 human impact ------
# Human.Impacts.One.Off.Impacts Human.Impacts.Continuous.Impacts

# max of each
# DAF = 0
# O  = 0.4
# R  = 0.8
# Absent = 1

long_plots$human_impact_cover <- pmax(
  long_plots$Human.Impacts.One.Off.Impacts,
  long_plots$Human.Impacts.Continuous.Impacts,
  na.rm = TRUE
)
long_plots$WECA_human_impact_value <- case_when(
  long_plots$human_impact_cover == "Absent" ~ 1,
  long_plots$human_impact_cover == "R" ~ 0.8,
  long_plots$human_impact_cover == "O" ~ 0.4,
  long_plots$human_impact_cover %in% c("F", "A", "D") ~ 0
)

plot_av_bysurvey_human_impact <- long_plots %>%
  group_by(id) %>%
  summarise(
    WECA_human_impact_value_plotav = mean(WECA_human_impact_value, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

overall$human_impact_cover <- pmax(
  overall$Human.Impacts.One.Off.Impacts,
  overall$Human.Impacts.Continuous.Impacts,
  na.rm = TRUE
)
overall$WECA_human_impact_value_overall <- case_when(
  overall$human_impact_cover == "Absent" ~ 1,
  overall$human_impact_cover == "R" ~ 0.8,
  overall$human_impact_cover == "O" ~ 0.4,
  overall$human_impact_cover %in% c("F", "A", "D") ~ 0
)
overall <- overall %>%
  select(-any_of("WECA_human_impact_value_plotav")) %>%
  left_join(plot_av_bysurvey_human_impact, by = "id")

# plot score 2
# overall score 1.5


```

Plot of human impact value, comparing mean of plots to overall. There is a strong and relatively 1:1 relationship.
